- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% of forecasted range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overreacts; cap forecast at 70–72 unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to account for volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks in early-to-mid period; shift forecast upward by 1–3% for days 1–10 if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts; adjust forecast slope to match sentiment swing direction.
